details.summary: This is an outstanding, book-ready recipe. It elegantly handles the stringent dessert constraints by using plain Greek yogurt and vanilla extract to avoid the added sugars of commercial flavored yogurts, delivering a comforting, compliant dish within the 30-minute ceiling.

dimensions.feedback: Classic, comforting combination of apples, cinnamon, nutmeg, maple, and pecans. The flavor profile is perfectly balanced and coherent.
All ingredients are correctly listed and properly utilized in the instructions.
Instructions are excellent. The bake time provides a functional range (15 to 20 minutes) with a clear visual doneness cue ('tender and lightly browned') and a mid-point check.
The recipe aligns perfectly with a Modern American dessert profile, mimicking apple pie flavors.
Baking 1/4-inch apple slices on parchment at 400°F works well. The parchment is critical here to prevent sticking since the recipe doesn't use oil to coat the apples.
The computed nutrition values are highly accurate and align perfectly with the ingredient weights.
The title and intro accurately describe the dish. The intro uses a warm, practical tone without any disallowed health or 'diet' claims.
A highly appealing, realistic weeknight dessert that feels satisfying without being overly heavy.
Excellent adherence to the mandate. High-quality fruit carbohydrates and lean Greek yogurt protein create a dessert that respects both blood sugar and liver health.

Brilliant execution of the sugar constraint. By flavoring plain Greek yogurt with vanilla extract instead of using pre-sweetened commercial vanilla yogurt, the added sugar stays extremely low (2.4g) while retaining the intended flavor. The 25.8g carbohydrate load is high-quality and falls nicely into the target window.
A perfect fit for the Desserts chapter. It easily hits all nutrient targets (protein > 4g, carbs in the 14-28g window, added sugar well under 7g) and matches the expected fruit/dairy-forward style.

Prep takes about 10 minutes, which perfectly overlaps with the oven preheating. A 15-minute bake brings this to the table right at the 25-30 minute mark. Ingredients are standard pantry staples available at any supermarket.
